LESSON: GRAMMAR IN USE 15.3.1 AFFIRMATIVE AND NEGATIVE SENTENCES

Grade: Grade 7
Subject: ENGLISH
Strand: Strand 15
Topic 15.3: Grammar in Use 15.3.1 Affirmative and Negative Sentences
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Grammar in Use 15.3.1 Affirmative and Negative Sentences, part of Strand 15 in Grade 7 ENGLISH.

Key inquiry question: When do we use affirmative statements? 2. When do we use negative statements? 3. Why is it important to use the right sentence when saying something?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. search online and offline for the differences between affirmative and negative sentences and share them with peers,

2. role-play a dialogue with affirmative and negative sentences and record themselves,

3. watch/listen to a conversation on issues like tourist sites in Kenya and pick out the affirmative and negative sentences,

4. sort jumbled up sentences into affirmative and negative sentences,

5. construct affirmative and negative sentences,

6. share sentences made in the form of charts for peer review, 1.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. search online and offline for the differences between affirmative and negative sentences and share them with peers,
2. role-play a dialogue with affirmative and negative sentences and record themselves,
3. watch/listen to a conversation on issues like tourist sites in Kenya and pick out the affirmative and negative sentences,
4. sort jumbled up sentences into affirmative and negative sentences,
5. construct affirmative and negative sentences,
6. share sentences made in the form of charts for peer review, 1.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Grammar in Use 15.3.1 Affirmative and Negative Sentences together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Citizenship: It is enhanced in using critical inquiry as learners make affirmative and negative sentences on the tourist

attraction sites in Kenya.

• Digital literacy: It is developed as learner uses digital devices to search online and offline for the differences between

affirmative and negative sentences and shares them with peers.

Values:
• Unity is enhanced as learners share sentences made in the form of charts for peer review.

• Patriotism is enhanced as the learner nurtures love for own country by reading texts on tourist attraction sites.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs)

• Citizenship Education is enhanced through texts on tourist sites in Kenya.

• Creative Thinking is enhanced as learners create dialogue and stories using declarative sentences.

Link to other Learning Areas:

The learner relates the concept of affirmative and negative sentences to their learning of language use in Kiswahili.
